a) To allow the writ petition and direct the respondent to consider the reply filed by the petitioner and pass a detail order for demolition found illegal.

c) A writ, direction or order in the nature of mandamus or as deemed fit be issue directing the respondent to compensate the petitioner (legal owners of the property)
under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
d) Any other relief, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in favour of the petitioner.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner's land was acquired by the respondent NHAI in the year 2009 for the purpose of construction of National Highway and granted compensation to the petitioner.
Thereafter, the respondent authority demarcated the land of the petitioner which was not acquired by them.
The petitioner got the building constructed after getting due permission and sanction.

However, of late the authorities are now trying to demolish the property of the petitioner without any authority of law and without deciding the reply of the petitioner and wants to encroach upon the land without following the process as mentioned in the Act of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, therefore, the respondent needs to be restrained from taking any illegal action against the petitioner.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the record.
5.
On perusal of the writ petition, it is seen that no show cause notice or any notice to demolish/demarcate the land has been issued by the respondent to the petitioner.
Merely, on the basis of apprehension this petition has been filed.
It is a settled legal position that the petitions cannot be entertained on mere apprehension.

6. In view of the aforesaid, this Court is not inclined to entertain this writ petition and, accordingly,
the same is dismissed in limine.
However, the petitioner would be at liberty to approach again in case some illegal action is taken by the respondent against the petitioner.
7. With the aforesaid liberty, the writ petition stands disposed of.

(S. A. DHARMADHIKARI)
